theme: How many more: match them up and count who is left

activities.title: Who is left with nobody
activities.intro: Two groups every time. One group is already sitting up here at the top. Give every one of them a partner from the pile, one each, and then tell me how many in the pile are left with nobody.
activities.offScreen: Go and find four spoons and seven forks. Give every spoon one fork, then tell a grown up how many forks got left over.

rounds.prompt: Four cups up here. Now look at the fish. Give every cup one fish. How many fish are left with no cup?
Five blocks up here. Give every block one bird. How many birds are left with no block?
Six cups up here. Give every cup one coin. How many coins are left with no cup?
Seven rocks up here. Give every rock one leaf. How many leaves are left with no rock?

activities.title: A little bit more than these
activities.intro: One pile is sitting up at the top for you to look at. Count it out loud. Then find the pile down below that has just a few more than it, and tap that one.
activities.offScreen: Build a tower of five blocks, then go and build one that has two more than that, and show somebody both towers.

rounds.prompt: Five stars up here. Tap the pile of coins that has exactly two more than the stars.
Three blocks up here. Tap the pile of leaves that has exactly two more than the blocks.
Six fish up here. Tap the pile of birds that has exactly one more than the fish.
Four cups up here. Tap the pile of flowers that has exactly three more than the cups.

activities.title: Who is ahead, and by how many
activities.intro: Two piles. Count them both, then tap the one that is ahead. After you tap, say out loud how many more it has. Saying it is the fun part and nobody is checking it.
activities.offScreen: Ask a grown up to make two little piles of anything, and you get to say which pile is ahead and by how many.

rounds.prompt: Six coins and nine coins. Tap the pile that is ahead, then say out loud how many more it has.
Eight birds and five birds. Tap the pile that is ahead, then say out loud how many more it has.
Four leaves and seven leaves. Tap the pile that is ahead, then say out loud how many more it has.
Ten blocks and six blocks. Tap the pile that is ahead, then say out loud how many more it has, and then go and tell somebody.

parentCard.title: The counting song, once slow and once silly
steps: Sit on the floor facing each other with your hands free. Sing five little ducks together, or any counting song they already love, and put up a finger for every duck so the number is always visible on your hands.

At the end of a verse, freeze. You hold up your ducks and they hold up theirs, different numbers, and ask the question of the week: who has more, and how many more? Let them find it by touching your fingers to theirs, one to one, and counting the ones with nobody to touch.
Sing the whole song again, silly this time. Too fast, squeaky voices, ducks that quack the numbers. Freeze at the same places and ask the same question, and let them ask it back to you at least once.

Then make it real. Two little piles on the floor, socks or spoons or blocks, one pile yours and one theirs. Line them up side by side and count the leftovers together. Do it three or four times, and let them choose the piles.
Finish by letting them invent a verse. Any animal they like and any number up to ten, sung once through, and you have to work out who is ahead and by how many while they watch you do it.
notice: When they compare two piles, do they line them up one to one, or do they count each pile from one all over again?
Do they answer more without a number, and does the number come if you wait instead of asking again?
Do they start noticing gaps on their own at other times, at the table or in the bath, without anybody starting the game?
